title: Malignant hyperthermia crisis
subject: anaesthesia
summary: Suspect MH with unexplained rising end-tidal CO2, tachycardia and rigidity after a volatile agent or suxamethonium. Stop triggers, hyperventilate with 100% O2, give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV as a rapid bolus and repeat until controlled, cool, treat hyperkalaemia and acidosis, and monitor in critical care for at least 24 hours.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Triggers: all volatile anaesthetics (sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane, halothane, methoxyflurane) and suxamethonium. It can occur even after previous uneventful anaesthetics.

Early signs: unexplained rising end-tidal CO2 despite increased ventilation (tachypnoea if spontaneously breathing), rising O2 consumption, mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis, sweating, mottled skin.
Cardiovascular: inappropriate tachycardia, ventricular ectopics or bigeminy, unstable blood pressure.
Muscle: masseter spasm after suxamethonium, generalised rigidity.
Later signs: hyperkalaemia, rapidly rising core temperature, very high CK and myoglobin, dark urine (myoglobinuria), severe arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, DIC. Fever is often a late sign.

Differentials: light anaesthesia, sepsis, inadequate ventilation or fresh gas flow, machine fault, anaphylaxis, phaeochromocytoma, thyroid storm, laparoscopic CO2 absorption, recreational drugs, neuroleptic malignant or serotonin syndrome.

sections.title: Immediate actions
items: Declare an emergency, call for help and get dantrolene and the MH kit. Ask the surgeon to finish or abandon surgery as fast as possible.
Stop all triggers. Remove the vaporiser; do not waste time changing the machine or circuit. Insert activated charcoal filters in the inspiratory and expiratory limbs if available.
Hyperventilate with 100% O2 at high fresh gas flow (at least 10 L/min), minute volume 2 to 3 times normal.
Maintain anaesthesia with non-trigger agents (TIVA: propofol, opioids, non-depolarising blockers).
Give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV as a rapid bolus (actual body weight; EMHG 2 to 2.5 mg/kg, max 300 mg per dose) through a large-bore line, giving each syringe as soon as it is ready.

Then give 1 mg/kg IV every 5 minutes (Association of Anaesthetists 2020), or repeat the full dose every 10 minutes (EMHG 2024), until end-tidal CO2 and PaCO2 fall (under 6 kPa with normal minute ventilation) and core temperature is falling.

sections.title: Dantrolene and secondary features
items: Dantrolene 20 mg vials: reconstitute each with 60 mL sterile water for injection (not saline or glucose); a 70 kg adult needs 7 to 9 vials per dose. Ryanodex 250 mg vials: 5 mL sterile water each. Assign two or more people to mix.
Up to 1200 mg (60 vials of 20 mg) may be needed in an adult. Reappraise the diagnosis at a cumulative 10 mg/kg; if MH is still likely, keep giving dantrolene beyond it with specialist advice.
Cooling: 2000 to 3000 mL of chilled (4 to 8 C) IV crystalloid plus surface cooling; stop active cooling once core temperature is below 38.5 C to avoid overshoot.
Hyperkalaemia (K above 5.9 mmol/L or ECG changes): calcium chloride 10 mg/kg IV (max 2 g) or calcium gluconate, insulin with glucose, salbutamol, and haemofiltration or dialysis if refractory.
Acidosis: ventilate to normocapnia; give sodium bicarbonate 1 to 2 mmol/kg IV if pH is below 7.2.
Arrhythmias: amiodarone or magnesium; beta-blockers for persistent tachycardia. Do not use calcium channel blockers (they interact with dantrolene).
Keep urine output above 1 mL/kg/h (above 2 mL/kg/h if myoglobinuria) with crystalloid and furosemide; alkalinise urine if CK or potassium keep rising.

sections.title: Monitoring and critical care
items: Core temperature, ECG, invasive arterial pressure, urinary catheter; consider central venous access.
Frequent arterial blood gas, potassium, glucose, CK, myoglobin; renal and liver function and coagulation (DIC). Look for compartment syndrome.
Monitor in ICU or critical care recovery for at least 24 hours: about 25% relapse, and relapses can be fatal.

Recurrence: repeat dantrolene 2 to 2.5 mg/kg every 10 minutes. Many centres continue dantrolene 1 mg/kg IV every 4 to 6 hours for 24 hours (MHAUS); stop or space it when metabolically stable for 24 hours, temperature under 38 C, CK falling, no myoglobinuria and no rigidity.

sections.title: Children and special situations
items: Children: same weight-based dantrolene regimen as adults (2.5 mg/kg, then repeat doses until controlled). Hyperkalaemia: insulin 0.1 units/kg IV with glucose (for example 2 mL/kg of 25% dextrose), calcium chloride 10 mg/kg (max 2 g).
Sudden hyperkalaemic cardiac arrest after suxamethonium in a young boy suggests an undiagnosed myopathy (for example Duchenne): treat the hyperkalaemia with calcium, insulin-glucose and CPR.
Isolated masseter spasm after suxamethonium: abandon volatiles if possible, monitor closely for MH, check CK and urine myoglobin, and refer for investigation.

sections.title: Preparedness and follow-up
items: Every site that uses volatile agents or suxamethonium should keep dantrolene immediately available: EMHG advises 36 vials of 20 mg at once and a further 24 within 1 hour. In India stocks are often limited: know your nearest supply.

Keep a locally adapted MH treatment card with the dantrolene. Patients known or suspected to be MH-susceptible get trigger-free anaesthesia (no prophylactic dantrolene) with a prepared machine or charcoal filters.

After a crisis: explain to the patient and family, label the records as MH-susceptible, advise a medical alert, and refer the patient and relatives to an MH investigation unit (contracture testing or RYR1 or CACNA1S genetics).

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting for hyperthermia before diagnosing MH: rising end-tidal CO2 and tachycardia come first.
Under-dosing or slow delivery of dantrolene because too few people are reconstituting vials.
Changing the whole anaesthetic machine before giving dantrolene.
Forgetting that each 20 mg vial also contains 3 g mannitol, adding to diuresis.
Discharging to a ward too early; relapse can occur within 24 hours.

drugs.name: Dantrolene sodium
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg/kg IV rapid bolus (actual body weight; EMHG 2 to 2.5 mg/kg, max 300 mg per dose), then 1 mg/kg every 5 minutes (or the full dose every 10 minutes, EMHG) until controlled
drugs.notes: Reappraise the diagnosis at 10 mg/kg; it may need to be exceeded (up to about 1200 mg in adults). 20 mg vial plus 60 mL sterile water; Ryanodex 250 mg plus 5 mL sterile water. Same mg/kg in children.

drugs.name: Dantrolene (post-crisis)
drugs.dose: 1 mg/kg IV every 4 to 6 hours for at least 24 hours
drugs.notes: MHAUS regimen; watch the IV site for thrombophlebitis and extravasation.

drugs.name: Calcium chloride 10%
drugs.dose: 10 mg/kg IV (max 2 g) for hyperkalaemia with ECG changes
drugs.notes: Calcium gluconate if calcium chloride is unavailable.

drugs.name: Insulin with glucose
drugs.dose: Adult: 10 units regular insulin IV with 50 mL of 50% glucose. Child: 0.1 units/kg with 2 mL/kg of 25% glucose

drugs.name: Sodium bicarbonate
drugs.dose: 1 to 2 mmol/kg IV if pH below 7.2 or marked base deficit

drugs.name: Chilled crystalloid
drugs.dose: 2000 to 3000 mL IV at 4 to 8 C in adults
